content: When uploading a picture, navigate to the designated upload page. If the image originates from Radiopaedia, you must complete the image summary section on the upload page using the provided example as a guide. When citing a website, adhere to the following format: Title of the page Website title (date) Available at URL Accessed on Month Day, Year For citing a peer-reviewed article, search for the PMID or DOI on PubMed. Once located, use the citation creator tool to generate the appropriate reference. If the reference lacks a PubMed ID or DOI, apply the AMA referencing style as demonstrated in the examples below: For journal articles with 1-6 authors: Example: Hu P, Reuben DB. Effects of managed care on the length of time that elderly patients spend with physicians during ambulatory visits. Med Care. 2002;40(7):606-613. For journal articles with more than six authors: Example: Geller AC, Venna S, Prout M, et al. Should the skin cancer examination be taught in medical school? Arch Dermatol. 2002;138(9):1201-1203. For journal articles with no named author or group name: Example: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). MMWR Morb Mortal Wkly Rep. 2010;59(9):273. For electronic journal articles: Example: Gage BF, Fihn SD, White RH. Management and dosing of warfarin therapy. The American Journal of Medicine. 2000;109(6):481-488. doi:10.1016/S0002-9343(00)00545-3. When citing a book, locate the ISBN on platforms such as Amazon or Barnes & Noble. Input the ISBN into the citation generator, then copy the generated reference and enclose it within a reference tag. To create a table efficiently, utilize the wiki table generator tool. After generating the table, format it according to the rules outlined in the provided example. Use only the approved tags, preferably limiting the selection to one tag unless multiple are necessary.
